title: Auth API 401/429 debugging scratchpad - Samir 2026-03-03
content:
Goal: quickly triage recurring 401 + 429 responses hitting the hosted API (noticed since ~2026-03-03 02:50 UTC). This is a personal scratchpad to collect commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

Summary of observed behaviour:
- Clients intermittently receive 401 Unauthorized and 429 Too Many Requests for the same API key.
- 401s pattern: mostly for keys issued to internal service accounts and some long-running user sessions. 429s appear across many keys but concentrated in a few customer tenants.
- Time window: spike observed starting ~2026-03-03 02:50 UTC, ongoing but rate has decreased after rolling restart of auth-proxy (03:40 UTC).

Commands / requests I ran (examples):
1) Basic curl that returned 401:
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
--- response snippet ---
HTTP/2 401
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: req_abc123

{"error":{"message":"Invalid API key","type":"authentication_error"}}

2) Request that returned 429 with headers:
curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-OTHER"
--- headers ---
HTTP/2 429
content-type: application/json
retry-after: 30
x-rate-limit-limit: 60
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1677840000

{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit_error"}}

3) Test against auth proxy (local debug node):
curl -v http://auth-proxy.internal:8080/validate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED"
-- result: 200 OK for that key on the local proxy (so key not universally invalid)

Server / proxy logs (excerpt):
- 2026-03-03T02:50:12Z auth-proxy[pid=1123] WARN invalid-signature user=svc-analytics path=/v1/generate req=req_aa11
- 2026-03-03T02:50:15Z auth-proxy[pid=1123] ERROR token-expired key=sk-live-REDACTED user=svc-payment req=req_aa12
- 2026-03-03T03:02:31Z nginx[pid=2234] 10.0.1.12 - - [03/Mar/2026:03:02:31 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 401 123 "-" "Go-http-client/1.1"
- 2026-03-03T03:03:00Z rate-limiter[pid=987] INFO token-bucket depleted tenant=acct-772 xrl=0

Observed patterns / quick hypotheses:
- Mixed causes: some 401s are legit (expired/rotated keys), others are returned by the auth-proxy erroneously when backend session store (Redis) intermittently flaps.
- 429s: looks like token-bucket exhaustion on a per-tenant limit. x-rate-limit-remaining=0 + retry-after present supports token-bucket enforcement.
- There is a race between key rotation job (daily key-roll) and the auth cache TTL; if rotation occurs and cache hasn't been invalidated properly, we might serve 401s for a short window.
- Another hypothesis: misconfigured rate-limiter config after the deploy on 2026-03-02 (PR infra/auth-proxy#432) tightened the per-key burst and accidentally applied stricter per-tenant limits.

Evidence collected to date:
- Reproduced 401 from a client outside the internal network; same key validated locally against auth-proxy's debug endpoint -> implies problem upstream (edge / CDN) or differences in signed request verification at edge.
- Rate-limiter logs show a cluster-wide spike in token-bucket depletion at 02:50-03:10 UTC.
- No billing anomalies for affected keys (checked invoices/usage for a subset) -> suggests not quota exhaustion at billing layer.

Tried mitigations so far (and results):
- Restarted auth-proxy nodes in us-east1 (03:40 UTC) -> immediate drop in 401 incidents for internal svc keys, but 429s persisted for some customer tenants.
- Temporarily increased rate-limiter burst for tenants acct-772 and acct-811 (via K/V in config store) -> reduced 429s for those tenants, but other tenants started hitting limits, indicating global config may be too conservative.
- Rolled back infra/auth-proxy#432 on a staging subset to confirm behavior (manual test) -> confirmed that previous config allowed higher bursts.

Steps to reproduce consistently (approx):
1) Use a recently rotated key (simulate rotation by setting expiry flag in DB)
2) Send ~100 concurrent short generation requests (seq length small)
3) Observe 401s for some requests and 429s once concurrent volume exceeds token-bucket burst
\Immediate next actions (priority ordered):
- [Samir] Collect full auth-proxy metrics from 02:30-04:00 UTC (histograms, connection errors, redis timeouts).
- [Lena] Pull rate-limiter config change history and diff the deploy that merged infra/auth-proxy#432. (linked PR above)
- [Jamie] Check CDN/edge layer signing logic and verify that the edge isn't dropping Authorization header for certain keepalive connections.
- [Aisha] Cross-check tenants that got 429s against per-tenant override list in Consul / config-store to make sure no accidental default was applied.
- [Oncall SRE] Consider short-term relaxing of per-tenant burst limits for affected tenants using the safe kill-switch path in ops runbook (we used this earlier 2026-02-10).

Longer-term follow-ups / questions for product/security:
- Do we want a per-key vs per-tenant limit hierarchy? Current implementation favors per-tenant which can cause noisy neighbor issues. We should validate product requirements.
- Key rotation: should we use a grace window and dual-key acceptance for X minutes post-rotation to avoid transient 401s? (proposal: accept old key for 5 minutes and emit warning in logs).
- Adopt a clearer telemetry correlation: log request-id + backend auth-eviction-reason so we can trace 401s to either 'expired', 'signature', 'cache-miss', or 'redis-error'.

Notes / breadcrumbs for postmortem if this becomes an incident:
- Timestamps: spike start 2026-03-03T02:50:12Z, mitigations started 2026-03-03T03:40Z.
- Config changes to investigate: infra/auth-proxy#432 (deployed 2026-03-02 22:10 UTC), rate-limiter config commit abcdef (2026-03-02 21:55 UTC).
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12345/p1640000000.000000 (see pinned logs by Lena)
- Potential owners for postmortem: eng-serving-runtime + eng-sre + product-hosted-api

Quick debug checklist (for next person picking this up):
- Verify key: curl to auth-proxy internal debug endpoint -> should return 200 for valid key. If not, fetch auth-store record.
- Check Redis (auth cache) stats: look for evictions, connection errors, increased latency.
- Pull rate-limiter metrics: count of token-bucket refills, per-tenant drop rates, 429 rate by API route.
- Reproduce with a local load generator (wrk or k6) with same client headers to see edge differences.

Misc notes / random findings:
- Found one suspicious pattern: some clients send both Authorization: Bearer and X-Api-Key headers; edge routing rewrites caused the Authorization header to be removed in some keepalive flows (Jamie investigating).
- There was a partial rollback of a CDN rule on 2026-03-01 that might change header handling for long-lived connections.

Action items (concise):
- [ ] Samir: metrics dump + attach to JIRA-2217 (due EOD 2026-03-04)
- [ ] Lena: config diffs + callout to infra team on PR #432
- [ ] Jamie: edge header handling verification + small repro script
- [ ] Aisha: tenant config validation + temporary overrides for affected tenants

If you pick this up: start at the top of this file, run the curl examples, then follow the quick debug checklist. Add any logs/curl output you capture to this doc (append below) so we keep a single timeline.

-- end scratchpad --
